data.name: Performance_Body
data.value: Asks Windows to reclaim memory that running processes aren't actively using. Windows already does this automatically when something needs the memory, so the real-world effect is often modest. The numbers below are the actual measurement, not a promised gain.

data.name: Startup_Body
data.value: Apps that launch when Windows starts. Turning one off doesn't uninstall it, it just stops launching automatically, and can be turned back on any time. Only your own account's entries are shown, not shared system-wide ones.

data.name: Drivers_Body
data.value: Installed drivers and how old they are. Nothing here is downloaded or installed automatically, use Windows Update or the manufacturer's own site to update anything.

data.name: Drivers_DetailExplanation
data.value: A driver lets Windows and this device talk to each other correctly. Manufacturers release updates over time to fix bugs, improve compatibility, and sometimes close security issues. This one hasn't been updated in a while, which isn't necessarily a problem, but it's worth checking if the device works fine and you're not troubleshooting anything related to it. Updating is optional, only do it if you have a specific reason to (a problem with the device, or wanting the latest features).

data.name: Drivers_DetailOpenPrompt
data.value: Open {0}'s site to check for an update?

data.name: Browsers_Body
data.value: Clears cache, cookies, and browsing history for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox. Bookmarks and saved passwords are never touched. For Firefox, history is not offered here since it's stored together with bookmarks in the same file. Close your browsers first for best results.

data.name: Browsers_Cleaning
data.value: Cleaning, this can take a while for large caches...

data.name: Browsers_RiskLegend
data.value: Green: nothing meaningful is lost. Orange: minor inconvenience (signed out of sites). Red: something you might want to keep (history).

data.name: System_Body
data.value: Clears your Temp folder (low risk, files go to the Recycle Bin) and empties the Recycle Bin (medium risk, permanent, review what's in it first if unsure).

data.name: Uninstall_Body
data.value: Installed programs, largest first. Uninstalling runs each program's own official uninstaller, the same one Windows would run, nothing here deletes files or registry entries directly.

data.name: Uninstall_ConfirmBody
data.value: Uninstall {0}? This opens that program's own uninstaller, follow its prompts to finish.

data.name: Uninstall_LaunchFailedBody
data.value: Couldn't start the uninstaller for this program. It may need to be removed from Windows Settings > Apps instead.

data.name: Update_Available
data.value: A new version is available: v{0}

data.name: Update_DownloadFailedBody
data.value: The update couldn't be downloaded or installed. This can happen if your connection dropped, or if you declined the Windows security prompt for the installer (look for a "Windows protected your PC" message, click "More info" then "Run anyway"). You can also download the latest version manually from the website or GitHub.

data.name: Settings_Subtitle
data.value: Preferences are saved locally on this device.

data.name: Settings_LanguageRestartNote
data.value: Restart PurgeCore to apply a language change.

data.name: Settings_CookieWhitelistNote
data.value: One domain per line (e.g. gmail.com). When cleaning cookies in Cleanup, these are kept so you stay signed in. Leave empty to clear all cookies for the selected browsers.

data.name: Privacy_StaysLocal_Body
data.value: Drive, folder, and file names and paths, file sizes, types and dates, and every scan result stay on this computer. The scan engine reads your file system directly, there is no server involved in analyzing a disk.

data.name: Privacy_NeverCollected_Body
data.value: Your name, email, or Microsoft account. File names, paths, or contents. Folder names or structure. Detailed disk contents. Any identifier used to fingerprint this device. Usage analytics or telemetry of any kind, there is no opt-in analytics feature. There is no hidden or undocumented telemetry.

data.name: Privacy_Offline_Body
data.value: PurgeCore works fully offline. Disabling your internet connection does not affect scanning, results, or any core feature.

data.name: Privacy_Affiliate_Body
data.value: The NordVPN card on the Dashboard and the DeleteMe suggestion after a scan are affiliate links, clearly labeled where they appear. Clicking one opens your browser to the partner's site, which then applies its own privacy policy. PurgeCore does not track which links you click.

data.name: About_BetaNote
data.value: PurgeCore is in beta. The core features are stable, but it hasn't had wide real-world testing yet, expect the occasional rough edge.
